title: Ibn Mas'ud aloud
hook: the small shepherd Abdullah ibn Mas'ud recites Surah ar-Rahman aloud at the Ka'ba and is beaten (sirah)

segments.voice: Yesterday, Yasir's family on the hot ground, and a sentence for people he couldn't rescue. Your line was: patience, family of Yasir.

A small circle of the Prophet's companions in Mecca, talking low. Ibn Ishaq gives their worry in a sentence: Quraysh have never heard this Qur'an recited openly to them. Who will make them hear it? One voice answers: I will. It belongs to Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, a shepherd, slight and thin-legged, with no strong clan behind him. The others object; they want someone whose family will step in if the crowd turns on him. He goes anyway. Today: Ibn Mas'ud.
screen: `WHO WILL MAKE THEM HEAR IT?` → `"I WILL."` → `A SHEPHERD WITH NO CLAN.`

segments.voice: The next morning, Ibn Ishaq says, he goes to the Ka'ba while the leaders of Quraysh sit in their meeting places, stands at the Maqam, and raises his voice. He chooses the opening of surah fifty-five, ar-Rahman. In Pickthall's words: "The Beneficent Hath made known the Qur'an." Notice the choice. Not a warning, not a threat. A surah that opens with the name of mercy and lists gifts: the sun and moon, the sky raised up, the fruit and the palm, with a refrain that keeps coming back: "Which is it, of the favours of your Lord, that ye deny?" The crowd works out what he is reading, and they get up and strike him in the face. He keeps reciting as far as he can, then goes back to his friends, his face marked. They say: this is what we were afraid of. His answer, in Ibn Ishaq: God's enemies were never smaller in his eyes than now, and if they like, he'll do it again tomorrow. One more detail, from Musnad Ahmad. Once, some companions laughed at how thin Ibn Mas'ud's legs were, and the Prophet said those legs would weigh heavier on the scale than the mountain of Uhud. Put the two together: the man some laughed at carried the words of mercy out loud, paid for it, and offered to go back.
screen: `AT THE MAQAM, IN THE MORNING.` · `HE CHOSE AR-RAHMAN.` · `STRUCK IN THE FACE, STILL RECITING.` · `THIN LEGS, HEAVY ON THE SCALE.`

segments.voice: Choose a few lines that matter to you, a verse, a prayer you already know, a poem, a line your grandmother used to say, and say them in your full voice, slowly, so each word lands. If your voice shakes, let it shake. Then sit quietly and notice how the room sounds after.
Ar-Rahman, the Beneficent: the surah Ibn Mas'ud chose to recite aloud at the Ka'ba, naming God's mercy before the crowd that beat him for it. Today's word.
Your line: he recited it aloud. He chose words of mercy, and said them where it cost him. That's day seven hundred thirty-nine.

howItsDone: Muslims recite the Qur'an aloud in prayer and in gatherings, and Ibn Mas'ud is remembered among the companions known for their recitation.

chat.says: Why did Ibn Mas'ud recite surah ar-Rahman out loud at the Ka'ba?
options: So Quraysh would hear the Qur'an openly; he chose a surah opening with mercy.
To answer a dare from Quraysh to prove he could recite Arabic poetry.
Because he was told to warn Quraysh of a punishment coming that day.
chat.meaning: The companions worried Quraysh had never heard the Qur'an recited openly. Ibn Mas'ud went, and chose a surah that opens with the name of mercy.

Ibn Ishaq frames this as the first open recitation of the Qur'an to Quraysh by someone after the Prophet; the script says only 'never heard openly recited to them' as the companions' worry. The trapdoor floor says 'the first open recitation by a companion', attributed to Ibn Ishaq; confirm or soften.
Musnad Ahmad number (3991) cited from memory; confirm.
'Shepherd' rests on the report that he herded for Uqba ibn Abi Mu'ayt; 'slight' and 'thin-legged' from the Ahmad report. Confirm.
'A refrain that comes back again and again' avoids giving a count; confirm.
howItsDone calls him 'one of the great reciters among the companions' (cf. Bukhari's report naming him among those to learn the Qur'an from); confirm or soften.
